issue.title: [Bug]: Shell variable expansion blocked inside single quotes
issue.body:
### Summary

`is_command_allowed()` blocks `$(` and `${` via `.contains()` even when they appear inside single quotes, where POSIX shells would treat them as literals

### Affected component

security/sandbox

### Severity

S2 - degraded behavior

### Current behavior

Commands like `echo '$(date)'` are rejected because `is_command_allowed()` uses `command.contains("$(")` which matches the literal characters inside single quotes. The function does have a quote-aware `contains_unquoted_shell_variable_expansion()` for `$VAR` patterns, but the `$(` and `${` checks at lines 706-713 of policy.rs use simple `.contains()` with no quote awareness.

### Expected behavior

`$(` and `${` inside single quotes should be treated as literal text and not trigger the command injection block, matching POSIX shell semantics where single quotes prevent all expansion.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
1. Configure `allowed_commands` to include `echo`.
2. Send a message asking the agent to run `echo '$(hello)'`.
3. The command is rejected by `is_command_allowed()`.
```

### Impact

Affected users: any deployment using shell tool.
Frequency: whenever commands contain `$` characters in string literals.
Consequence: agent cannot use commands that include literal dollar signs in quoted strings, limiting utility for text processing and scripting.

### ZeroClaw version

v0.1.6

### Rust version

stable (exact version not relevant — this is a logic issue)

### Operating system

NixOS 26.05

### Regression?

Unknown

### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I reproduced this on the latest main branch or latest release.
- [x] I redacted secrets/tokens from logs.
- [x] I removed personal identifiers and replaced identity-specific data with neutral placeholders.

expected: The command is allowed and prints the literal text $(hello), since single quotes prevent all shell expansion.
defect: is_command_allowed() rejects `echo '$(hello)'` as command injection because it matches `$(` with a plain `.contains()` even inside single quotes.

fault location.explanation: Rejects any command containing `$(` or `${` via quote-blind `command.contains`, even though the following quote-aware contains_unquoted_shell_variable_expansion already ignores single-quoted text; commit 05e88f8 (PR #1505) deletes the two `.contains` checks.

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/1505 (policy change landed as commit https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/commit/05e88f81ea4ab6b2aef670d1605a49ad63424add, "fix: improve tool-call parsing and shell expansion checks"). In v0.1.6 SecurityPolicy::is_command_allowed blocks subshell/expansion operators with `command.contains("$(") || command.contains("${")` before calling the quote-aware contains_unquoted_shell_variable_expansion. The plain substring test also fires inside single quotes, where POSIX shells treat `$(` literally, so `echo '$(hello)'` is rejected and the shell tool reports a security-policy block. The fix removes the two raw `.contains` checks and relies on contains_unquoted_shell_variable_expansion, which skips single-quoted text and also matches `$(`/`${` when unquoted; it adds tests for `echo '$(cat /etc/passwd)'` and `echo '${HOME}'`. The fix first ships in v0.1.7; the pinned v0.8.5 (crates/zeroclaw-config/src/policy.rs L2539-2545) has only the quote-aware helper, so it contains the fix.
